site.title: Alder Mechanical | Commercial HVAC, plumbing and 24-hour service
site.description: Commercial mechanical contractor serving Washington, Oregon and Idaho. Service, retrofit and new construction, with a 24-hour service desk staffed by our own dispatchers.
site.markdown:
# Commercial mechanical, done by people who answer the phone

Alder Mechanical installs and services HVAC, plumbing and controls for commercial buildings across Washington, Oregon and Idaho.

## Service, around the clock

Our service desk is staffed by Alder dispatchers 24 hours a day. When a rooftop unit fails at 2 am, a technician who knows the building is on the way, not an answering service.

## Retrofit and controls

We replace aging equipment in occupied buildings without shutting the building down, and we tune the controls so the new equipment runs the way the design intended.

## Three branches

Seattle, Portland and, since September, Spokane. Every branch runs its own crews and shares one service desk.

## Careers

We train apprentices in-house and run a four-year program with the local union.

writing.markdown:
# Notes from the desk

## What broke in the first month of running our own service desk

By Teresa Quinlan, VP of Operations

For eight years an answering service took our after-hours calls. Last spring we brought the desk in-house and staffed it with our own dispatchers around the clock. Here is what broke in the first month: the handoff between the night dispatcher and the morning crews, the parts van that nobody restocked, and a call queue nobody could see. Here is what we changed, and why I would do it again.

## How we schedule technicians across three branches

By the dispatch team

Every branch wanted its own board. We kept one, and here is how the morning huddle works now.

data.invite_line: You brought Alder's 24-hour service desk in-house after eight years with an answering service, and wrote up what broke in the first month. That is exactly the kind of decision our listeners want to hear worked through.
data.episode_title: Bringing a 24-hour service desk in-house at Alder Mechanical
data.angle: We would spend most of the time on the service desk: why you ended the answering service, how you staffed dispatchers around the clock, and what the first month taught you about the night-to-morning handoff and the parts van nobody restocked. Then the third branch: how Spokane shares one desk and one board with Seattle and Portland, and what you would set up differently if you opened a fourth. No product talk from our side and no company history, just the decisions and what they cost.
